rawItems.title: Reform councillor arrested over alleged false statements in election papers
rawItems.content: A Reform UK council group leader in Cambridgeshire has been arrested on suspicion of making false statements in election nomination papers. Representing the Ramsey Ward, Ryan Coogan was elected to Huntingdonshire District Council in the local elections on May 7. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed a man was arrested on September 24 on suspicion of making false statements in nomination papers. The 42-year-old from Waterbeach has since been released on bail to return to Milton Police Station on December 22. Coogan told The Hunts Post he has "worked and will continue to work with the police as part of the investigation". It comes after the force revealed it had launched an investigation into the alleged false statements shortly after the May election. A spokesperson said the inquiry relates to Coogan and the most recent election, though it has not disclosed the nature of the alleged statements. At the time, a spokesperson for Huntingdonshire District Council said: "We are aware of a police referral in relation to the recent district council elections. "As this matter is a live investigation, it would not be appropriate for the council or the returning officer to comment further at this stage." Coogan previously ran as Reform UK's candidate in the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough mayoral election, coming second last year. He was among the party's first representatives on the district council, winning his seat along with two other Reform candidates to represent the Ramsey ward. A

A village pub near Ramsey has won retrospective permission to keep a static caravan, converted horsebox and swimming pool. The application relates to The Dog and Castle in Woodwalton and sought permission for a static caravan used as living accommodation, a converted horsebox used for guest accommodation, and a swimming pool with a raised deck area. The facilities have already been installed at the site. Council planners concluded the development would help support the continued operation of the village pub and restaurant and would not cause unacceptable harm to the character of the area, neighbouring residents or highway safety. The swimming pool can stay say planners, but there are time conditions on its use. (Image: HDC) Documents submitted for applicant John McGinn said the pub was an important community facility and the extra accommodation and leisure facilities would boost its income. The planning statement said the site already had guest accommodation approved in 2002. The application also explained that the static caravan is occupied by the pub landlord because a recent accident has left them unable to access the first-floor flat above the pub due to mobility difficulties.
